title: Adding PBS to LAP reagent bottle
description: A laboratory operator wearing green gloves prepares a chemical solution by adding PBS to a small brown bottle containing LAP. Three micropipettes are held on the pipette stand: two already have tips attached and one has no tip. The operator opens the PBS bottle, retrieves the micropipette without a tip, opens the pipette tip box, attaches a fresh tip, aspirates PBS, and dispenses it into the brown bottle. A magnetic stirrer with a beaker of water runs continuously in the background.

prompt_for_gen: From a nearby observer viewpoint, a laboratory workspace is visible featuring a black benchtop. In the center, a magnetic stirrer operates continuously, agitating a glass beaker filled with clear water. To the left, a pipette stand holds three micropipettes: two already have tips attached, while one has no tip. A closed box of pipette tips sits behind the stirrer. The operator, wearing green nitrile gloves, holds a small brown glass bottle in the left hand. The right hand unscrews the white cap of the brown bottle and sets it aside to expose the opening. The operator then reaches with the right hand to a large plastic bottle of PBS buffer on the right side of the bench and unscrews its cap. Next, the right hand retrieves the untipped micropipette from the stand, opens the pipette tip box, attaches a fresh tip, and inserts the tip into the PBS bottle to aspirate a volume of liquid. Finally, the operator moves the pipette over the open brown bottle and dispenses the PBS into it, mixing the buffer with the reagent inside. The video concludes with the liquid successfully transferred into the brown bottle.
